name: StorageClasses & dynamic provisioning
objective: CKA › Storage. Drill EVERY storage corner harder than the exam: StorageClasses (provisioner, reclaimPolicy, binding mode), static PVs with a retain reclaim policy, explicit static PVC binding, mounting a PVC, subPath mounts, the default-class annotation, dynamic provisioning via the default class, and a no-hint diagnose-and-fix. Graded exactly, per requirement.

questions.title: StorageClass: provisioner, reclaimPolicy, binding mode
questions.teach:
A cluster-scoped **StorageClass** names a `provisioner` (the driver), a `reclaimPolicy` (`Delete`/`Retain`) applied to PVs it creates, and a `volumeBindingMode` (`Immediate` or `WaitForFirstConsumer`, which delays binding until a pod schedules).

**Gotcha:** `reclaimPolicy` and `volumeBindingMode` are **immutable** — to change them you must delete and recreate the class.
questions.prompt:
Create a StorageClass `fast-local` with provisioner `rancher.io/local-path`, `reclaimPolicy: Delete`, and `volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer`.

Target: `kubectl get sc fast-local` shows that provisioner, reclaim policy, and binding mode.
questions.hint: StorageClass manifest (apiVersion `storage.k8s.io/v1`) with top-level `provisioner`, `reclaimPolicy`, and `volumeBindingMode`, then `kubectl apply -f -`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: fast-local
provisioner: rancher.io/local-path
reclaimPolicy: Delete
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer
YAML

verification.description: StorageClass fast-local: provisioner rancher.io/local-path, reclaimPolicy Delete, WaitForFirstConsumer

questions.eli5:
In the static labs, an admin built lockers (PVs) by hand. That doesn't scale. A **StorageClass** is like a **vending machine for lockers**: instead of someone manually installing a locker, a user drops in a request and the machine **builds a brand-new locker on demand**. This is **dynamic provisioning**.

A StorageClass has three important settings:

- **`provisioner`** — which machine/driver actually makes the storage (here `rancher.io/local-path`). Think of it as the brand of vending machine.
- **`reclaimPolicy`** — what happens to a locker the machine built once its renter leaves. `Delete` = throw it away (and its data). `Retain` = keep it. This policy stamps every locker the machine produces.
- **`volumeBindingMode`** — *when* the machine builds the locker. `Immediate` = build it the moment someone asks. `WaitForFirstConsumer` = **wait** until a pod that will actually use it gets scheduled, *then* build the locker right where that pod landed. That placement-awareness is why you often want `WaitForFirstConsumer` for node-local storage.

**Watch out for:**

- `reclaimPolicy` and `volumeBindingMode` are **immutable** — you cannot edit them on an existing class. To change either, **delete and recreate** the StorageClass.
- The StorageClass `reclaimPolicy` applies **only** to PVs the class **dynamically creates**, not to any hand-made static PV.
- The `provisioner` string must match a driver that's actually **installed and running** in the cluster, or claims never get fulfilled.
- A StorageClass is **cluster-scoped** — no namespace.
questions.deepDive:
## StorageClasses & dynamic provisioning — full rundown

### Mental model
A **StorageClass (SC)** is a **cluster-scoped** template that describes *how to provision storage on demand*. When a PVC references a class (or uses the default) and no matching PV exists, the class's **provisioner** creates a PV automatically — **dynamic provisioning**. The SC also stamps the **reclaim policy** onto every PV it creates and decides **when** binding happens via **volumeBindingMode**.

### Minimal StorageClass
```yaml
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: fast-local
provisioner: rancher.io/local-path       # top-level, NOT under spec
reclaimPolicy: Delete                     # Delete | Retain
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer   # Immediate | WaitForFirstConsumer
# allowVolumeExpansion: true
# parameters: { type: ssd }
```
Note: a StorageClass has **no `spec:`** — `provisioner`, `reclaimPolicy`, `volumeBindingMode`, `parameters`, `allowVolumeExpansion`, and `mountOptions` are all **top-level** fields.

```bash
kubectl apply -f sc.yaml
kubectl get sc
kubectl get sc fast-local -o wide
kubectl describe sc fast-local
```

### The key fields
| Field | Values | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `provisioner` | e.g. `rancher.io/local-path`, `kubernetes.io/no-provisioner`, a CSI driver | which driver creates volumes |
| `reclaimPolicy` | `Delete` (default) / `Retain` | policy stamped on **dynamically created** PVs |
| `volumeBindingMode` | `Immediate` (default) / `WaitForFirstConsumer` | when the PV is provisioned/bound |
| `allowVolumeExpansion` | `true` / `false` | whether PVCs on this class can grow |
| `parameters` | driver-specific map | e.g. disk type, fsType, IOPS |
| `mountOptions` | list | mount flags for created volumes |

### volumeBindingMode — the exam favourite
| Mode | When binding/provisioning happens | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `Immediate` | as soon as the PVC is created | simple; but can bind a volume in the wrong zone/node before the pod is scheduled |
| `WaitForFirstConsumer` | only once a **pod using the PVC is scheduled** | the provisioner places the volume on the **right node/zone** for that pod — essential for `local`/topology-constrained storage |

With `WaitForFirstConsumer`, a freshly created PVC sitting at `Pending` **before** any consumer pod exists is **expected**, not a failure.

### reclaimPolicy here vs on a PV
- SC `reclaimPolicy` → applied to PVs the **class provisions dynamically**.
- A **static** PV's own `persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy` governs that hand-made PV; the SC does not touch it.

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **`reclaimPolicy` and `volumeBindingMode` are immutable.** To change them you must **delete and recreate** the StorageClass (existing PVs keep the policy they were born with).
- **No `spec:` block** — putting `provisioner` under `spec` is a common mistake.
- **`provisioner` must be a driver actually installed** in the cluster; otherwise PVCs stay `Pending` ("waiting for a volume to be created").
- `kubernetes.io/no-provisioner` means **no dynamic provisioning** — used for static/`local` volumes that you pre-create.
- StorageClass is **cluster-scoped** (no namespace).
- The **default** reclaim policy if omitted is `Delete`; default binding mode is `Immediate`.

### Quick reference
```bash
kubectl get sc                                            # list; marks (default)
kubectl get sc fast-local -o jsonpath='{.provisioner} {.reclaimPolicy} {.volumeBindingMode}'; echo
kubectl delete sc fast-local && kubectl apply -f sc.yaml  # to change immutable fields
```

questions.title: Mark a StorageClass as the cluster default
questions.teach:
A PVC that **omits** `storageClassName` uses the cluster's **default StorageClass**. Mark a class default with the annotation `storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class: "true"` (via `kubectl patch` or `annotate`); `kubectl get sc` then flags it `(default)`.

**Gotcha:** the value must be the quoted **string** `"true"`, and only one class should carry it — two defaults is an error.
questions.prompt:
Mark StorageClass `fast-local` as the cluster default via the `storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class` annotation.

Target: `kubectl get sc` shows `fast-local (default)`.
questions.solution:
kubectl patch storageclass fast-local -p '{"metadata":{"annotations":{"storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class":"true"}}}'
kubectl get sc
questions.eli5:
Imagine a building with several vending machines (StorageClasses). When someone asks for a locker **but doesn't name a machine**, which one serves them? Whichever one is marked as the **house default**.

Marking a StorageClass as the cluster default is exactly that: you stick a sticker on one machine that says *"use me when nobody picks."* The sticker is an **annotation**:

`storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class: "true"`

You add it with `kubectl patch` (or `kubectl annotate`). Afterward, `kubectl get sc` shows your class with a friendly **`(default)`** tag next to its name. Now any PVC that leaves out `storageClassName` quietly gets handled by this class.

**Watch out for:**

- The value has to be the **quoted string `"true"`**, not a bare boolean. Annotation values are always strings, so `true` without quotes can bite you.
- **Only one** StorageClass should be the default at a time. If two carry the sticker, Kubernetes gets confused and a class-less PVC may fail to get a class assigned.
- "Default" only kicks in when a PVC **omits** `storageClassName` entirely. A PVC that sets `storageClassName: ""` (empty string) is explicitly saying *"no class, no dynamic provisioning"* — that's different from omitting it.
- To **remove** the default, patch the annotation back to `"false"` (or delete it).
- The annotation goes under `metadata.annotations` on the StorageClass.
questions.deepDive:
## The default StorageClass — full rundown

### Mental model
A PVC that **omits** `storageClassName` is assigned the cluster's **default StorageClass** at admission time. You designate the default by putting the annotation `storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class: "true"` on exactly **one** StorageClass. `kubectl get sc` then shows it tagged `(default)`.

### Setting it
```bash
# patch (strategic merge)
kubectl patch storageclass fast-local \
  -p '{"metadata":{"annotations":{"storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class":"true"}}}'

# equivalent with annotate
kubectl annotate sc fast-local storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class="true" --overwrite

kubectl get sc        # fast-local (default)
```

In YAML:
```yaml
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: fast-local
  annotations:
    storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class: "true"   # quoted string!
provisioner: rancher.io/local-path
```

### Unsetting / switching
```bash
# clear the default
kubectl patch sc fast-local \
  -p '{"metadata":{"annotations":{"storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class":"false"}}}'
```
To move the default, set `"false"` on the old class and `"true"` on the new one — never leave two defaults.

### How class resolution works for a PVC
| PVC `storageClassName` | Result |
|---|---|
| set to a name | that class is used |
| **field omitted** | the **default** class is injected (if one exists); if none, PVC has no class |
| `""` (empty string) | **no** class, **no** dynamic provisioning — binds only to PVs with `storageClassName: ""` |

> Omitting the field and setting it to `""` are **different**. `""` opts out of the default on purpose.

### The annotation
| Annotation | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class` | `"true"` / `"false"` | current key |
| `storageclass.beta.kubernetes.io/is-default-class` | `"true"` | legacy/deprecated, still honoured on old clusters |

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **Value must be the quoted string `"true"`.** Annotation values are strings; an unquoted boolean is a YAML/JSON error or mis-type.
- **Only one default.** Multiple defaults is an error — the admission plugin may refuse to pick, leaving class-less PVCs unassigned/`Pending`.
- **Default only applies to PVCs that omit the field.** `storageClassName: ""` explicitly disables it.
- Changing the default **does not retroactively** change existing bound PVCs — only new, class-less PVCs.
- The annotation is on the **StorageClass's `metadata.annotations`**, not the PVC.

### Quick reference
```bash
kubectl get sc                                     # which one shows (default)
kubectl get sc -o jsonpath=\
'{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{"\t"}{.metadata.annotations.storageclass\.kubernetes\.io/is-default-class}{"\n"}{end}'
```

questions.title: Dynamic provisioning via the default class
questions.teach:
A PVC with **no** `storageClassName` is handled by the default class and **dynamically provisions** a PV. Because `fast-local` is `WaitForFirstConsumer`, the PVC stays `Pending` until a pod that uses it is scheduled — only then does it bind.

**Gotcha:** with `WaitForFirstConsumer`, seeing the PVC `Pending` before any consumer exists is **normal**, not a failure — create the consuming pod to trigger binding.
questions.prompt:
In namespace `storage-learn`:
- create PVC `dyn-pvc` requesting `500Mi`, accessModes `ReadWriteOnce`, with **no** `storageClassName` (so it uses the default).
- create pod `dyn-app` (`busybox:1.36`, `sleep 3600`) that mounts `dyn-pvc` at `/data` to trigger binding.

Target: `dyn-pvc` becomes `Bound` and pod `dyn-app` is `Running`.
questions.hint: Omit `storageClassName` entirely on the PVC (do NOT set it to ""). Then the pod referencing it via `persistentVolumeClaim.claimName: dyn-pvc` triggers the WaitForFirstConsumer bind.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: dyn-pvc
  namespace: storage-learn
spec:
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 500Mi
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: dyn-app
  namespace: storage-learn
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep","3600"]
    volumeMounts:
    - name: data
      mountPath: /data
  volumes:
  - name: data
    persistentVolumeClaim:
      claimName: dyn-pvc
YAML
kubectl -n storage-learn wait --for=condition=Ready pod/dyn-app --timeout=90s

verification.description: dyn-pvc is Bound (dynamically provisioned via default class) and dyn-app is Running

questions.eli5:
Now you put it all together with the **vending machine** you set as the house default.

You fill out a rental slip (a **PVC**) but **leave the machine name blank** — no `storageClassName`. Because there's a default machine, Kubernetes hands your slip to it. You ask for `500Mi` and single-node read-write access. So far, nothing has actually been built.

Why not? Because your default class (`fast-local`) is set to **`WaitForFirstConsumer`** — "wait for the first customer." The machine refuses to build the locker until it knows **which pod** will use it and **where** that pod lands. So the PVC sits at **`Pending`**, and that's **completely normal** at this stage, not a bug.

The moment you create the pod (`dyn-app`) that mounts the claim, the scheduler places the pod, the machine builds a fresh locker right there, binds it to your claim — PVC flips to **`Bound`** — and the pod goes **`Running`**.

**Watch out for:**

- **Omit `storageClassName` entirely**. Do **not** set it to `""` — empty string means "no class, no dynamic provisioning," and your PVC would never bind.
- With `WaitForFirstConsumer`, a `Pending` PVC **before** any pod exists is expected. Don't panic and don't "fix" it — just create the consumer pod.
- The pod is the **trigger**. No consumer pod means no binding, forever.
- The PVC and the pod must be in the **same namespace** (`storage-learn`).
- You get a locker stamped with the class's `reclaimPolicy` (`Delete` here) — so deleting the PVC later **destroys** the data.
questions.deepDive:
## Dynamic provisioning via the default class — full rundown

### Mental model
Create a PVC with **no** `storageClassName`; the **default StorageClass** is injected, and its provisioner **creates a PV on demand**. When the class uses **`WaitForFirstConsumer`**, provisioning/binding is deferred until a **pod that mounts the PVC is scheduled** — so the volume lands on the node the pod runs on.

### The two objects
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: dyn-pvc
  namespace: storage-learn
spec:
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 500Mi
  # NOTE: storageClassName intentionally OMITTED -> uses default
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: dyn-app
  namespace: storage-learn
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep","3600"]
    volumeMounts:
    - name: data
      mountPath: /data
  volumes:
  - name: data
    persistentVolumeClaim:
      claimName: dyn-pvc
```
```bash
kubectl apply -f dyn.yaml
kubectl -n storage-learn get pvc dyn-pvc        # Pending until pod schedules, then Bound
kubectl -n storage-learn get pod dyn-app -o wide
kubectl get pv                                  # a new PV auto-created, named pvc-<uid>
```

### Lifecycle with WaitForFirstConsumer
| Step | State |
|---|---|
| PVC created, no consumer | PVC `Pending` (normal), no PV yet |
| Consumer pod created | scheduler picks a node |
| Pod scheduled | provisioner creates a PV on/for that node |
| Bind completes | PVC `Bound`, pod `ContainerCreating` → `Running` |

With `Immediate` mode, the PV would be provisioned the instant the PVC is created, before the pod exists.

### storageClassName: omit vs "" (critical)
| PVC setting | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| **field omitted** | default class used → **dynamic provisioning** |
| `storageClassName: ""` | **opt out** of default; **no** dynamic provisioning; binds only to a PV also set to `""` → stays `Pending` here |
| `storageClassName: fast-local` | explicitly that class |

### Verifying the bind
```bash
kubectl -n storage-learn get pvc dyn-pvc -o jsonpath='{.status.phase}'; echo   # Bound
kubectl -n storage-learn get pvc dyn-pvc -o jsonpath='{.spec.volumeName}'; echo  # pvc-<uid>
kubectl -n storage-learn describe pvc dyn-pvc | sed -n '/Events/,$p'
```

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **Must OMIT `storageClassName`** to use the default — setting `""` disables provisioning and the PVC never binds.
- **`Pending` before a consumer is normal** under `WaitForFirstConsumer` — the pod is the trigger; don't treat it as broken.
- **No default class defined?** A class-less PVC stays `Pending` forever (`no persistent volumes available / no storage class`).
- **PVC + pod must share a namespace.**
- The dynamic PV inherits the class's `reclaimPolicy` (`Delete` here) → deleting the PVC **deletes the data**.
- Auto-created PVs are named `pvc-<claim-uid>`.

### Quick reference
```bash
kubectl -n storage-learn get pvc,pod
kubectl -n storage-learn wait --for=jsonpath='{.status.phase}'=Bound pvc/dyn-pvc --timeout=90s
kubectl -n storage-learn wait --for=condition=Ready pod/dyn-app --timeout=90s
```
